hypotheses.justification: This follows from hx and the construction of C.Q. Prove by QuasiTab.build.induct that every type-three subtree of build inC step Hist Γ has its label in inC: build_of_leaf has no such subtree; build_of_node creates its type-three node only under Γ ∈ inC, and recursive subtrees satisfy the induction hypothesis. Apply this invariant using QuasiTab.mem_subtrees_of_atOpt hx and the definition of LoadedCluster.Q, then retain the original proof. The invariant also covers type-three nodes with no children.

Split on Δ.basic. The non-basic case uses the existing proof. In the basic case, hS.basicStep supplies Y with C.stepOf Δ = {Y}, hence C.stepOfL Δ = [Y] by the definitions of stepOfL and Finset.pdlSeqSort. Then hlen gives next.length = 1, hlab gives the child's label Y, and IH supplies SatDown for that child. Apply the preceding lemma satDown_three_basic. The length equality excludes an empty next in this branch.

The proof only needs i < next.length for the index supplied by nonBasicStep. This follows from hlab i hi and hx: if next.length ≤ i, List.getElem?_eq_none, QuasiTab.atOpt_append, and the definitions of atOpt and labelAt make C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) equal none, contradicting hlab i hi. Replace the omega step with this argument; everything else is unchanged. If the step list is empty, nonBasicStep already contradicts the satisfiability antecedent.

hypotheses.binder: (hlab : ∀ i, (hi : i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length) → C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) = some ((C.stepOfL Δ)[i]'hi))
hypotheses.justification: Recover hlab from hx by a construction invariant: every type-three subtree q of build inC step Hist Γ satisfies q.children.map QuasiTab.label = step q.label. Prove this by QuasiTab.build.induct using build_of_node, build_of_leaf, and QuasiTab.build_label; the newly created children are precisely builds of the step labels. Apply it to hx using QuasiTab.mem_subtrees_of_atOpt and LoadedCluster.Q. For each hi, hlen supplies the corresponding next index, and QuasiTab.atOpt_child plus labelAt gives hlab. Empty step lists require no indices. The original proof then applies.
